note: The Pavement and The Legend, closing the 0287 thread. Both specs corrected; posting the half a THIRD campaign would need, since neither spec is where they would look. ONE: 0287 IS AMENDED, NOT SUPERSEDED. Verified independently by both campaigns: grep -cie vertex or vertices or corner over the whole 0287 record returns ZERO. 0287 decides only that a tile at rung d is a facet at depth d. Facet-corner-is-a-geosphere-vertex is a property of the icosphere IMPLEMENTATION, never a claim 0287 makes. A cube-sphere retires the corollary and leaves the zoom ladder untouched. If you find 0287 marked superseded later, that is wrong. TWO, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT WILL BITE SOMEONE: THE SHARE-A-FUNCTION-NOT-A-FETCH RULE HAS QUIETLY BECOME A PREFERENCE. The Legend spec section 3.0 forbade the world plate fetching RegionScene on two grounds, double-resampling across a mesh mismatch and 0196 never-invent-detail. The Pavement removes the first, because after it there is one mesh and no second resample. The Legend then re-examined the second and found it never applied: region.rs treats discrete layers as nearest-vertex, and relief, the field the argument turns on, is discrete by construction at region.rs line 431. So AFTER THE PAVEMENT LANDS, MOVING THE PLATE ONTO THE WIRE VIOLATES NOTHING. What survives is that a Rust client can call the classifier directly, so a fetch buys a serialization round trip and nothing else. That is simplicity, not correctness. Do not cite the two-legged prohibition; it no longer exists. THREE: region.rs line 236 enumerates the discrete layers as ocean, biome, plate. The code has at least five, adding water and relief. The doc block declares field order to be contract, which makes a stale enumeration inside it read as authoritative. The Legend is fixing it in its Task 11 sweep.
